---
title: "Opportunity & routine activity"
toc: true
---

## Motivation (stylized facts)
::: {.callout-note title="Stylized facts this mechanism aims to match"}
- Crime is concentrated in places (hotspots) and changes with routine patterns and guardianship.
- Some interventions reduce crime by reducing opportunity rather than changing preferences.
:::

## Mechanism
The opportunity perspective treats crime as requiring:
- a motivated offender,
- a suitable target,
- absence of capable guardianship.

Academic implication: you can reduce crime by changing the **environment of opportunity** (visibility, access, guardianship), even holding preferences fixed.

## Canonical modeling primitives
- offenders choose where/when to search (location choice)
- guardianship shifts detection risk
- targets differ in attractiveness
- displacement is possible (crime moves rather than disappears)

## Predictions (qualitative)
- increasing guardianship in a place reduces expected returns and shifts activity elsewhere unless there are frictions
- policies can change measured crime mechanically through visibility/reporting changes
- hotspot concentration can arise from heterogeneity in target density and guardianship

## Later-on analysis
- combine with deterrence: opportunity changes the benefit side ($b$) and/or detection probability ($q$)
- add spatial equilibrium: offenders allocate across locations until expected payoffs equalize (with frictions)
